title: Portable Harness installation and safe target-repository bootstrap

original_request.text: Quiero que este repositorio sea instalable en cualquier repositorio con una serie de comandos, de forma comparable a publicar una herramienta en npm, y quiero saber cómo hacerlo y si se migran y agregan todos los archivos al hacerlo instalable. Quiero que trabajes como corresponde creando sprint, epic, task specs y planning, todo lo necesario para realizar esta tarea, y quiero activar ese flujo porque antes no se siguió el flujo del harnes.
original_request.canonical_english: I want this repository to be installable into any repository through a set of commands, comparably to publishing a tool on npm. I want to determine how to do it and whether making it installable migrates and adds all files. I want the work to follow the harness flow by creating the sprint, epic, task specifications, and planning needed to deliver this capability, because that flow was not followed earlier.
original_request.back_translation: Quiero que este repositorio sea instalable en cualquier repositorio mediante una serie de comandos, de forma comparable a publicar una herramienta en npm. Quiero determinar cómo hacerlo y si hacerlo instalable migra y agrega todos los archivos. Quiero que el trabajo siga el flujo del harness creando el sprint, la épica, las especificaciones de tareas y la planificación necesarios para entregar esta capacidad, porque ese flujo no se siguió antes.

refined_problem: Repository maintainers need a supported command-line installation path that can add the Harness to an arbitrary target repository without overwriting target-owned files, leaking credentials, silently migrating existing configuration, or embedding an author-specific absolute checkout path in ACI or provider configuration.
target_users: Maintainers who want to adopt Harness in an existing repository
Release maintainers who package and distribute the Harness CLI
outcomes: A target repository can run a documented installer command.
The installer reports a deterministic plan before any file mutation.
Installed files, preserved target-owned files, and skipped conflicts are observable.
Installed ACI and provider configuration resolves from the target installation rather than an author machine path.

success_metrics.name: clean-target bootstrap
success_metrics.definition: A clean fixture repository receives the documented managed files and passes the Harness validation command.

success_metrics.name: ownership safety
success_metrics.definition: An existing target-owned or modified managed file is never overwritten without an explicit operator choice.

in: A private-Git distributable Python command-line package proposal from https://github.com/mar-romero/harness
Target-repository bootstrap, ownership manifest, dry-run, and collision behavior
Portable ACI and provider configuration that does not embed a source-checkout path
out: Copying source history, credentials, tasks, planning artifacts, runtime runs, caches, or user task data into targets
Automatic destructive migration of pre-existing target files

assumptions.statement: The repository is a Python project, so a Python distribution with a console-script entry point is the lowest-friction npm-like delivery option.
Installation should copy a defined managed template set, not the entire source repository; tasks, planning, runtime state, caches, and credentials are always excluded.
Installed configuration must derive its repository root from the target installation or an explicit operator-provided setting; it must not serialize an author-specific absolute checkout path.

open_questions.question: Distribution channel selected: private Git repository https://github.com/mar-romero/harness.
Target layouts selected: empty or existing Git repositories without Harness; an existing installation of this Harness version may be installed or updated only through its managed-file manifest.
Managed-file conflict policy selected: fail without mutating the target repository and report every conflict.

challenges.challenge: Packaging a CLI does not imply copying every repository file; the installation manifest must define ownership and exclusions.
Public package publishing and target-file overwrite behavior are human approval gates.
Desktop and MCP launchers must start from a target repository on Windows without relying on a path from the machine that created the package.

mvp.goal: Install a versioned Harness template into a clean or existing Git repository with dry-run and conflict-safe behavior.
includes: Python package and console entry point
Portable target-root resolution for ACI and provider configuration
Fixture tests for clean install and collisions

work_items.title: Portable Harness bootstrap
work_items.description: Deliver a safely distributed CLI that can bootstrap approved Harness files into a target repository.
success_criteria: The installer has an explicit ownership manifest and collision policy.
The distribution and migration boundaries are approved before implementation.

tasks.title: Package the Harness CLI, portable configuration, and managed-file manifest
tasks.description: Create the installable Python CLI package, portable ACI/provider configuration, and an explicit versioned manifest defining the files that may be installed into a target repository, with exclusions for tasks, planning, runtime state, caches, and credentials.
acceptance_criteria: The package builds from the private Git repository.
The CLI exposes a stable entry point and version metadata.
The manifest declares managed paths and explicit excluded paths.
Installed ACI and provider configuration resolves the target root without an author-specific absolute path.
A portable configuration test exercises an external working directory on Windows.
No target-repository mutation occurs in this task.

tasks.title: Implement safe install, update, and conflict failure
tasks.description: Implement dry-run and apply behavior for clean targets and same-version Harness updates, failing before mutation when a destination is unowned or modified.
acceptance_criteria: Clean and existing Git targets can be installed.
Same-version managed files can be updated.
Any conflict fails and leaves the target unchanged.

tasks.title: Verify distribution and target-repository boundaries
tasks.description: Add fixture integration tests and operator documentation for package installation, dry-run, clean install, update, conflict failure, and excluded repository data.
acceptance_criteria: Fixture tests cover clean, update, conflict, and dry-run paths.
Tests prove excluded paths are not copied.
Documentation contains private-Git installation and recovery commands.

proposed_sprint.goal: Deliver a privately installable Harness CLI with a manifest-first, conflict-safe target bootstrap.
rationale: Portable package/configuration and manifest unblock safe apply; fixture verification closes the end-to-end slice within the default 12-unit capacity.

planning_boundary.reason: The user approved materializing the planning artifacts. Implementation remains gated: activate an individual task only after an explicit request to begin its code changes.
